title: Between, Within and Around: inter-, intro-, circum- and peri-
short: inter- means between, intro- and intra- mean within, and circum- and peri- mean around.
trouble: inter- (between) is not intra- (within): an interstate highway crosses states; intrastate travel stays inside one.

blocks.html: These prefixes tell where something is. inter- means “between” or “among”: an international game is played between nations, and to interrupt is to break in between. intro- (and intra-) means “within”: to introduce is to lead someone in. circum- and Greek peri- mean “around”: a circumference goes around a circle, and a perimeter measures around a shape.

head: Word and meaning
Parts, and what they say
rows:
interlocutor
a person taking part in a conversation

inter- between + locut speak + -or one who
→ “one who speaks between (in a conversation)”

introspective
looking inward at one’s own thoughts and feelings

circumspect
careful to consider all risks before acting

circumlocution
using many words to avoid saying something directly
blocks.cap: Each word, what it means now, and its parts. Words in italics are familiar words that are not on the list.

blocks.title: Between or within?
blocks.q: An interstate highway and an intrastate bus route: which one stays inside a single state?
steps: inter- means between: an interstate highway runs between states.
intra- means within: an intrastate route stays within one state.

blocks.name: vo-word

entry.def: careful to think about risks before acting
entry.ex: A {circumspect} hiker checks the weather twice before setting out.
entry.ctx: Unlike his brother, who signed whatever was put in front of him, Nate was {circumspect}: he read every line of the lease and asked about each fee.
entry.etym: From Latin circumspectus, “cautious, well considered,” from circumspicere, “to look around”: circum (around) + specere (to look).

mn.text: Before Pip crosses the busy street, he looks all around: left, right and left again. Looking all around before you act is being {circumspect}.

scene.alt: A boy at a street corner looks left and right before crossing, while a car comes down the road.

blocks.cap: A word from the list: circumspect.

blocks.html: Mixing up inter- (between) and intra- or intro- (within). Interstate travel crosses from one state to another; intrastate travel stays inside one. An introspective person looks within, at their own thoughts, not between people.

A circumlocution “talks around” the point (circum-, around + locut, speak). Asked whether he broke the vase, a boy who says, “Well, objects in a house can sometimes move in unexpected ways…” is using circumlocution.
